name: Field2D_SpriteNode_DrawAndCheckViewBounds
summary: Draws the 2D sprite node and then refreshes its view-bounds/cull flag. It is used as a per-frame update callback, stored in the delegate descriptor at 0x00671BB4.
evidence: NEW: both callees are now named (Field2D_SpriteNode_Draw 0x005CA4A8 and Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds 0x005CA31C) and the function address appears as a data word at 0x00671BB4 next to the 0x0070D718 delegate invoke stub, so this is a sprite-node update callback, not a map 'overlay' update.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_CreateChipSprite
signature: void* maybe_Field2D_Map_CreateChipSprite(void* self, u32 arg2, void* builder)
summary: Rebuilds the map's chip sprite at +0xA0: drops the old object, then creates a tween-move sprite when the map chip-kind byte (+0x22 of *(*(self+8)+0x2B4)) is 2, otherwise a bob-and-heading sprite, passing the matching callback descriptor.
evidence: NEW: the function is a delegate target stored at 0x005CA540 beside Field2D_Map_CreateTweenMove (0x00671B14) and std_Delegate_Invoke5ArgsF; both builders are now named Field2D_Sprite_* and the branch reads the chip-kind byte. Both builder names are themselves tentative, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_ReleaseSpriteNode
summary: Releases the map sprite object at +0xA0 (virtual slot 0, then NULL) and re-initialises the inline node handle at +0x70 through Gfx_ReleaseNodeHandle. The two data references sit next to Field2D_Map_SetInlineDescriptorB, so this is a Field2D map-descriptor helper.
evidence: NEW: Gfx_ReleaseNodeHandle's readable body writes its wrapper vtable into the out pointer passed as its first argument, so the call on self+0x70 rebuilds an inline node handle and is not a generic 'overlay rebuild'; the old lettered wording was a placeholder. There is still no caller, so the exact map object role stays open.

name: Sys_InitTwoCriticalSections
summary: Zeroes and initialises the two adjacent 12-byte critical sections at 0x007E7954 and 0x007E7960 through Os_InitCriticalSection; the CONCAT44 in the old pseudocode was just the return-register pair.
evidence: NEW: both targets are BSS blocks, each zeroed and then passed to the now-named Os_InitCriticalSection; nothing is registered or looked up, so the old RegisterGlobal wording was wrong. It has no callers (a static initialiser), which is why it is not raised above 0.5.

name: maybe_Sys_InitTimingSlot
summary: One-time initialiser: calls 0x0010EBB0, zeroes the 3-word global at 0x007C8050 (third word -1), then registers (0x007AE174, 0x00509A18) through 0x0010E8C0 and stores 0x00780C14 in the returned slot.
evidence: NEW: the literal pool at 0x0069F2EC holds 0x00509A18, 0x007AE174 and 0x00780C14, so the old 'timestamp object at 0x007AE174' described only one literal; the body actually zeroes 0x007C8050. The helpers 0x0010EBB0/0x0010E8C0 are not decompiled, so the module (timing vs. OS registration) is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateChildPane
summary: Allocates a 0xC0-byte pane object (alignment 4, through 0x0053CF14) and binds the given pane's children into it. The only caller, Ui_MapWindow_BindPanes, uses it for the icon_jumon / null_icon_global bindings.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Ui_MapWindow_BindPanes and the constructor callee is the named Ui_LayoutPane_BindChildren; the previous '64-byte-aligned' note was wrong (the call is (0xC0, 4) to an unnamed allocator). The allocated object class is still generic, so maybe_ stays.

name: Container_ReleaseTripleBuffers
summary: Frees up to three owned buffers of a small container/path sub-object through the free helper 0x0010F69C and clears the following count word. Path_Dtor calls it once per path buffer head and Container_ReleaseListAndFree calls it on &self->f_10.
evidence: NEW: eight named callers (Path_Dtor, Camera_Dtor, Ui_MotionPath_Dtor, Field_Gimmick_BuildPathTable, Field_MultiPart_InitSpriteList, ...) all use it as the teardown of a sub-object that owns three separately allocated buffers; the body is exactly three operator-delete calls plus a zero count. 'List' was too narrow, hence the buffers wording.

name: Os_IpcSendSyncRequestCmd21
summary: Issues an IPC round trip with command header 0x00210000 (command 0x21, no parameters): writes the header into the thread's TLS block at +0x80, takes the session handle from the global 0x007AEAB0, executes svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest) and returns the reply word at TLS+0x84 on success.
evidence: NEW: the ARM body is mrc p15 (read TLS), str #0x210000 to [tls+0x80], ldr r0,[0x007AEAB0], svc 0x32, then ldrge r0,[tls+0x84]; so the handle is a fixed global and the function takes no arguments (the old pseudocode made the global look like the result). Caller Fs_MountDefaultArchives shows the archive-mount use; what driver command 0x21 means is still unidentified beyond the header value.

name: maybe_Os_IpcSession_PollAsyncState
summary: Polls the driver session at 0x007B2D08: reads the state bytes of the object at session+0xC, returns 0 or one of 0xF9610C02 / 0xC8A10C01 / 0xC8A10C0D / 0xC8810FEF depending on the state and pending counter, and re-issues command 0x19 when the counter is positive.
evidence: NEW: 0x007B2D08 is the driver-session struct whose handle is at +0x24 (0x007B2D2C, see Os_IpcSendCommand06), and 0x00123750 also clears its pending word. Both callers (Save_AsyncReadWorker 0x001170CC and maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker 0x00117458) are worker loops, so 'Save_CheckReadState' wrongly narrowed a shared IPC state machine; the state semantics remain unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_CompleteAsyncRead
summary: Completes an asynchronous save/load request: passes the five request fields at +0x14..+0x24 to Save_AsyncReadWorker and then stores state 5 in the shared work object 0x007B00E0, the worker's completion marker.
evidence: NEW: Save_AsyncReadWorker (0x001170CC) is the named worker and its doc confirms 0x007B00E0 is the shared completion state, so the body is a straight completion hand-off. No caller is readable, so the 'Complete' role is still inferred.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentThreadHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a thread handle queried through command 0x0B on the driver session, closing the previous handle with svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) first and aborting through 0x0011ED40 when the query fails.
evidence: NEW: the query helper is the named maybe_Os_IpcCmd0BGetThreadValue (0x001228FC) and the body closes the old value with svc 0x23 before storing the new one; the companion 0x00122440 does the same for command 0x0A. The public nn::os API name is still a reconstruction.

name: maybe_Os_GetCurrentProcessHandle
summary: Replaces *out with a process handle queried through command 0x0A on the driver session, closing the previous handle with svc 0x23 first and aborting through 0x0011ED40 when the query fails.
evidence: NEW: the helper is the named maybe_Os_IpcCmd0AGetProcessValue (0x00123C9C) and the caller maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry (0x00122650) shows it is needed by the read-retry path; the body is the exact process-side twin of 0x0011DF0C. The API name is still inferred.

name: maybe_Os_HandleInit
summary: Creates a kernel handle through 0x0012038C into an empty *out slot and aborts through 0x00118100 on failure; when *out is already non-NULL it deliberately aborts with 0xE0A0183B, so it is a create-once helper.
evidence: NEW: the initial result value 0xE0A0183B has bit 31 set and is reached when *out is already set, i.e. it is an invalid-state assert, not a second creation attempt. Callers (maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop, maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry, the two OS helpers) only need a fresh handle slot; the handle kind is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitIpcCommand430040
summary: Flushes the pending GPU callbacks (two inner entries of Os_InvokeCallbacks at 0x00118814), submits IPC command 0x430040 through Gfx_IpcCmd430040 and aborts through 0x00118924 on failure.
evidence: NEW: the ARM bytes at 0x00119DF8 are push {r4,lr}; bl 0x00119BA8; bl 0x001198CC; bl 0x0011A3B0; error check; pop {r4,lr}, and the function returns at 0x00119E14. The svcCloseHandle/svcWaitSynchronization half Ghidra printed in the same body belongs to a separate function at 0x00119E1C (hidden mid-symbol boundary), so 'SignalEvent' described that neighbour instead of this wrapper. Body is a merged/damaged decompilation, hence 0.35.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand06AndClearPending
summary: Forwards the selector byte to driver command 0x06 (Os_IpcSendCommand06), translates a non-success result through the 0x0011ED40 assert and then unconditionally clears the pending word at driver-session+4; called once per sampling iteration by 0x00122484.
evidence: NEW: the callee is the named Os_IpcSendCommand06 (0x00124C64, command header 0x00060040) and the caller is the per-sample loop 0x00122484; only the store to 0x007B2D08+4 is the 'clear pending' part, so the old IpcCmd06 name was incomplete rather than wrong.

name: Field_NpcMoveAction_Ctor
signature: void* Field_NpcMoveAction_Ctor(void* storage, void* npc, void* actionList, const char* tag, u32 slot)
summary: Constructor of the NPC 'move' action object (0x54 bytes): builds the ActorAction base through Field_ActorAction_CtorBaseA, installs vtable 0x0075C378 and seeds the movement defaults (-1, copied global pair, zeroed state fields).
evidence: NEW: its only caller Field_RegisterNpcActions allocates 0x54 bytes and passes the inline string 'move' (0x00180254, loaded into r3 at 0x00180134) for action slot 1; the installed vtable 0x0075C378 has Actor_InitBoundsCheck (0x002267EC) and Actor_InitStateController (0x002274B0), which matches a movement action. The extra r1..r3 arguments are dropped by Ghidra (register-forwarding trap).

name: Field_NpcNutAction_Ctor
signature: void* Field_NpcNutAction_Ctor(void* storage, void* npc, void* actionList, const char* tag, u32 slot)
summary: Constructor of the NPC idle ('nut') action object (0x2C bytes): runs Field_ActorAction_CtorBaseA and installs vtable 0x0075A4EC, the actor animation-timer class.
evidence: NEW: Field_RegisterNpcActions allocates 0x2C bytes and passes the inline string 'nut' (0x0018024C, loaded into r3 at 0x00180034) for action slot 0; the sibling slots are 'move' (slot 1), 'flw' (slot 2, 0x00180250) and 'talk' (slot 3). The installed vtable 0x0075A4EC has maybe_Actor_StartAnimTimer and maybe_Actor_UpdateAnimTimer, matching an animated idle action. Extra arguments are forwarded r1..r3 (Ghidra trap).

name: Field_NpcFlwAction_Ctor
signature: void* Field_NpcFlwAction_Ctor(void* storage, void* npc, void* actionList, const char* tag, u32 slot)
summary: Constructor of the NPC follow ('flw') action object (0x2C bytes): runs Field_ActorAction_CtorBaseA and installs vtable 0x0075FA64, whose behaviour slots include maybe_Field_Gimmick_SnapToNearbyActor.
evidence: NEW: Field_RegisterNpcActions allocates 0x2C bytes and passes the inline string 'flw' (0x00180250, loaded into r3 at 0x001800B4) for action slot 2; the vtable 0x0075FA64 contains maybe_Field_Gimmick_SnapToNearbyActor (0x002BD954) in its update slot and Field_Object_ReleaseChildList in the teardown area, which fits the follow behaviour. Extra arguments are forwarded r1..r3 (Ghidra trap).

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorThunkD
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: destroys the Ui layout sub-object base through 0x001B7DB0 and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is slot +0x38 of vtable 0x0075A4EC, the class constructed by Field_NpcNutAction_Ctor.
evidence: NEW: the ARM call at 0x001DC41C goes to 0x001B7DB0, an inner entry of Ui_Layout_DeleteSubComponentD (0x001B7DA0), so the base is a Ui layout sub-object; the owner vtable 0x0075A4EC also holds Ui_ListEntry_SyncSprite and Message_SetArgTextById. The concrete class cannot be told from the 16-byte body, so the lettered name stays.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor that first stores the vtable passed in r1, then runs the shared actor-action base destructor and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is the sub-object destructor slot of the Field actor-move task.
evidence: NEW: the function is slot +0x00 of vtable 0x0075A5C8, whose other slots are the named maybe_Field_ActorMove_Begin/End/Update/InitDirection/Cancel/Integrate family; the base-dtor call at 0x001E0D34 reaches 0x00294C24 (inner entry of the shared actor-action dtor 0x00294C14). The stored-vptr form makes this the base-subobject variant.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_DeletingDtorB
summary: Primary deleting destructor of the Field actor-move task: runs the shared actor-action base destructor and then releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is the slot-0 dtor of vtable 0x0075A5C8, next to maybe_Field_ActorMove_Begin/End/Update.
evidence: NEW: the function is the slot-0 pointer of vtable 0x0075A5C8, the same table as maybe_Field_ActorMove_Begin/End/Update/InitDirection/Cancel/Integrate, and the base-dtor call at 0x001E123C reaches 0x00294C24. Unlike 0x001E0D2C it does not store a vptr, i.e. this is the primary-object variant.

name: maybe_Object_DtorThunkF
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: destroys the base object through 0x002B0A04 (the Ui text-scroll-window base destructor) and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is slot 0 of vtable 0x0075B97C.
evidence: NEW: the ARM call at 0x00213130 goes to 0x002B0A04, an inner entry of maybe_Ui_TextScrollWindow_DtorDeleteB (0x002B09F4), and the owner vtable 0x0075B97C shares slots with Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub; so the class is a Ui widget derived from the text-scroll-window base. The concrete class is not recoverable from 16 bytes.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a Ui_Panel-derived widget: stores the vtable from r1, destroys the embedded Ui_Panel base at +0x2C through 0x002EA47C and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: NEW: disassembly at 0x002B13D0 calls 0x002EA47C (inner entry of maybe_Ui_Panel_DeletingDtor 0x002EA468) after storing the vptr at +0x2C, so the owner is a Ui_Panel-derived class rather than a generic 'Ui widget'. No rodata pointer to this function exists (it is reached through a computed table), so the concrete class stays unknown.

name: maybe_Field_Object_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a Field object derived from the Ui layout sub-component: runs the Ui layout base destructor 0x001B7A34 and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is the dtor slot of vtable 0x0075FA64.
evidence: NEW: the base-dtor call at 0x002BDABC reaches 0x001B7A34 (inner entry of Ui_Layout_DeleteSubComponentC 0x001B7A24) and the owner vtable 0x0075FA64 has maybe_Field_Gimmick_SnapToNearbyActor in its update slot and Field_Object_ReleaseChildList in its teardown area, so 'Field object' is supported but the concrete class is not identifiable.

name: maybe_Field_Action_DtorDeleteA
summary: Deleting destructor: runs the Field actor-action base destructor 0x00294C84 and then releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is slot 0 of vtable 0x0075FD64.
evidence: NEW: the base-dtor call at 0x002C0A18 reaches 0x00294C84 (inner entry of 0x00294C74) and the owner vtable 0x0075FD64 has Field_ActorAction_PlayStateAnim and Actor_Action_IvyNut_UpdateAnim in its following slots, so the Field actor-action family is supported; the concrete action still cannot be named.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small field actor-action/scene object: runs the shared Gfx object-desc base destructor 0x00193E44 and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is slot 0 of vtable 0x007625D8.
evidence: NEW: the 15 entries starting at 0x007625D8 end at 0x00762614, where the separate Field_CollisionObject vtable begins (Field_CollisionObject_DeletingDtor/Init), so this is a distinct non-collision class; its own table contains maybe_Field_ActorAction_CheckFacingTarget (0x0036D174). The 'gimmick' label remains a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_TweenSequence_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the tween-sequence object: stores the vtable from r1, destroys the base object through 0x002B0A04 and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x00764054 places it as slot 0 of the table whose +0x0C slot is maybe_Ui_TweenSequence_Update (0x0032B3DC), and the base-dtor call at 0x0032B62C reaches 0x002B0A04 (Ui text-scroll-window base). The only class-specific sibling is itself a maybe_ name, so the tween-sequence attribution is not strong enough to drop the prefix.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor of a Field actor action: runs the shared actor-action base destructor 0x00294C24 and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC. It is slot 0 of vtable 0x00768784, the move-to action class.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x00768784 is slot 0 of a table whose slots +0x10/+0x18 are ActorAction_UpdateMoveTo and maybe_ActorAction_ApplyCurvePosition, so the class is the move-to actor action; the base-dtor call at 0x003ADF58 reaches 0x00294C24. The lettered placeholder stays because sibling action classes share this exact shape.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_DeletingDtorG
summary: Deleting destructor of a Ui_Panel-derived widget: stores the vtable from r1, destroys the embedded Ui_Panel base at +0x2C through 0x002EA47C and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: NEW: disassembly at 0x003D5E48 calls 0x002EA47C (inner entry of maybe_Ui_Panel_DeletingDtor 0x002EA468) after the vptr store, so the object is a Ui_Panel-derived widget, not a Field actor action as the old prefix claimed. No rodata pointer identifies the concrete class.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_CalcPartyModelCenter
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_CalcPartyModelCenter(float* out, void* party, u32 attachment, u32 arg4)
summary: Counts the non-null members of the 16-slot party model array, gets each model's attachment world position (or the slot actor through maybe_PartyGroup_GetSlotActor) and writes the centre of the resulting bounds to *out.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_SpawnPartyEffect and the callees are Model_GetAttachmentWorldPosition and maybe_PartyGroup_GetSlotActor; the 16-slot loop plus the min/max accumulation over the returned world positions shows it computes a bounds centre, so 'Get' is too weak. One min/max term is still mangled by the decompiler (fVar7-fVar7), hence 0.4.

name: maybe_Ui_SelectSlotByRecordId
signature: void maybe_Ui_SelectSlotByRecordId(void* self, u32 recordKey, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Shared screen method: scans up to 0x55F rows from the data-manager lookup 0x0063FD24 for the first row whose +0x147 word equals the given key and selects that index (or 0xFFFF) through the screen's virtual slot +0xD8.
evidence: NEW: the function address appears at the same slot of twelve different battle/field screen vtables (e.g. 0x0075B53C, 0x0075CD7C, 0x0075E894, 0x00760974), always immediately before maybe_Battle_CollectModelChildren, so it is a shared Ui screen method rather than a list-specific helper. What the +0x147 key actually is remains unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_OnConfirm
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_OnConfirm(void* self, u32 p1, u32 p2, u32 p3)
summary: Confirm handler of the shop window: reads the two input managers' slot-0x30 state and, when both report the button, either sends command 0xD or sets state 6 and sends command 0x11 through the window's +0xC vtable.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0072B9DC sits in the shop-window table next to the named Ui_ShopWindow_OnSelectRowMode1 (0x00285904) and maybe_Ui_StopFadeAndSound (0x0072B9D4), so the old 'Pane' class was wrong. The combined two-button test and the 0xD/0x11 branch read as confirm-with-special-case, but the button pair is not identified.

name: Actor2D_AnimNodeCtor
summary: Constructor of the Actor2D animation/sprite node: allocates through 0x00335CA8, installs vtable 0x0075D55C, initialises the self-referencing list heads and the 0xFF/0xFFFF defaults, then constructs the embedded Actor_HandleRef child and returns the node base.
evidence: NEW: the installed vtable 0x0075D55C has Actor2D_AnimNode_DeletingDtor at +0x08 and Actor2D_ReRegisterObject at +0x10, so the class is the Actor2D animation node and the old 'Anim2D' prefix had the subsystem backwards. The body also builds the embedded Actor_HandleRef child (0x004AF3F4), which matches a 2D actor node.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObj_DeletingDtorA
summary: Deleting destructor of a field scene object: restores the embedded Actor2D node's vtable words, unlinks that node from its intrusive list, runs Field_Object_DtorBase on the embedded object at -0x24C and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: NEW: the vtable words written by the body are 0x0075D55C (the Actor2D anim-node table) and its +0x98 sub-table, so the object embeds an Actor2D node at +0x24C rather than being one; Field_Object_DtorBase is now named and the intrusive-list unlink is explicit. The concrete scene-object class is still unidentified.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_UpdateAnimation
summary: Per-frame driver of the dive-window animator: runs the base update, advances the 1/30 s timer at +0x140, dispatches the current 0x18-byte step record while +0x134 < 0x0B and clears the UI input-mode word when the +0x264 latch is set.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0075E1C4 is a slot of the table that also contains Ui_DiveWindow_DtorDeleteAlt (0x0029C418), Ui_DiveWindow_InitPanes (0x0029A5D4) and maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_ApplyChildState (0x0029A8E0), so the class is DiveWindow and the old 'FrameScript' wording was a placeholder. The step targets are still unrecovered.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNextArrow
summary: Timer-driven layout animation: while the window reports 'not busy' through virtual +0x4C it subtracts the 1/30 s frame delta from the float timer at +0x188 and, when the timer crosses zero, clamps it to -1 and tail-calls Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim on the child at +0x13C with the id (*(u16*)(self+0x164)<<16) and the callback 0x003239F4.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0076ACD0 sits in a message-window table that also holds Ui_MessageWindow_LoadLayout (0x003E0F70) and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseBase (0x003E10D4), and the tail call is the now-named Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim (0x001A6680), not a row-text setter. The third argument 0x003239F4 is an unnamed function used as the layout-animation callback (its prologue sits just past the nominal size of BattleScene_ModelSlotManager_Dtor), so the 'next arrow' use is still inferred and the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateAnimation
summary: Per-frame driver of the Smith-menu animator: while the animator is idle it advances the clock at +0xD94/+0xD98 by 1/30 s and then dispatches the current step out of the 13-entry table at +0xD8C.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0075DF7C sits beside maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateAnimStep (0x00298584) and maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_ReleaseMembers (0x002984A4), and the same table later contains Ui_SmithMenu_Init (0x00624B68); the body is the standard 0x18-byte step driver with the 0x3D088889 (1/30) delta, so both class and role are supported.

name: Ui_DiveForm_UpdateAnimation
summary: Per-frame driver of the dive-form animator: while the animator is idle it advances the clock at +0x357C by 1/30 s and dispatches the current step out of the 27-entry table at +0x3574.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0075E724 is in the DiveForm table that also holds Ui_DiveForm_BindControl (0x003BD750), maybe_Ui_Window_InitDataBinding (0x001DAABC) and Ui_BaseWindow_Close (0x003BE00C), so the class is proven; the body is the same generic 0x18-byte step driver with a 27-entry table. The individual steps stay unrecovered.

name: maybe_Ui_WindowStateSlot_Step
summary: Advances a window's two-entry state queue: when the current slot is idle it adds the 1/30 s frame delta to the slot timer and bumps the frame counter, then invokes the callback selected by +0x360 through the 0x18-byte entry and the adjustor table at +0x37C.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x00762C64 is next to maybe_Ui_WindowStateSlot_DispatchPending (0x00304804), and its table also holds maybe_Ui_NumberDisplay_RollDigits and Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim, so it is a window/number-display widget; the concrete class is still unknown. The two-entry dispatch body is unambiguous, but the exact entry field offsets are unclear, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_KyoukaiWindow_UpdateAnimation
summary: Frame update: accumulates the 1/30 s frame delta and, while the active slot index at +0xD90 is below 8, dispatches that slot's callback from the 0x18-byte entry using the dispatch table at +0xDAC.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x00768B8C sits in the KyoukaiWindow table next to Ui_KyoukaiWindow_CreatePanes (0x002CE7C8) and maybe_Ui_KyoukaiWindow_UpdateB (0x002CEA08); the body is the generic 0x18-byte step driver with a limit of 8. 'AnimQueue' described the mechanism but not the owning class, so the class prefix is corrected.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_UpdateQueue
summary: Frame update of a message-command window controller: accumulates the 1/30 s delta and, while the active slot index at +0xD90 is below 9, dispatches that slot's callback from the 0x18-byte entry using the dispatch table at +0xDAC.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x00768BEC sits in a table that contains maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_FlushQueue / ClearPaneFlag and Ui_ThreeRowNullTextWindow_Dtor / InitPanes, so the owner is one of the message-command / three-row text windows; the exact class cannot be separated, so the MessageCmd label stays tentative.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateAnim
summary: Frame update of the message window's animation controller at +0x8A4: optionally ticks the layout animation (+0x14C), advances the controller timer/counter when it is idle and dispatches the current of up to four 0x18-byte entries through the jump table at +0x8C4.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Ui_MessageWindow_Tick (0x001C5164) drives it, and the table at 0x0076AAC0 contains Ui_MessageWindow2_Ctor (0x003DE464), Ui_MessageWindow_SubDtor and Ui_MessageWindow_Part_Dtor; both the caller and the vtable agree on the message-window class, so the maybe_ prefix can be dropped.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_Update
summary: Per-frame update: releases finished child panes, then - depending on the state byte at +0x11C and the mode byte at +0x586 - asks the 2D object state-sequence runner (0x002D24BC) to advance the UI core's +0x14 manager.
evidence: NEW: the table at 0x0072B054 holds 0x0029AD34 / 0x0029B41C / 0x0029AC00, i.e. the same 0x0029Axxx DiveWindow block as 0x0029A920, and the call target 0x002D24BC is Field_Object2D_RunStateSequence. 'Update' is supported, but the +0x11C/+0x586 state gate is still unexplained.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion(void* self, int useNut, int seekLastFrame)
summary: Selects the actor's 'Nut' motion when useNut is non-zero (state word +0x288 = -1), otherwise the default 'Open' motion (+0x288 = 0), plays it through the animation owner at +0xB8 and, when seekLastFrame is set, jumps to the clip's last frame.
evidence: NEW: the inline literal at 0x002B342C is 'Nut' and the default name pointer is *0x007283F8, which resolves to the animation-name table entry 'Open' (0x007844C8: dead/Open/Fall_Loop/Sit_Loop/Move...); Ghidra printed 0x0074754E and 0x007283F8 as raw literals. The seek path uses the now-named Anim_Owner_Tick (0x002D19C8). Only the 'Npc' receiver label is inferred, and there is no caller.

name: Anim_Player_SetFrame
summary: Stores a frame index as a float in the animation player's +0x64 field, but only when a clip is attached at +0x44 and the frame lies in [0, clip frame count].
evidence: NEW: the caller Anim_Owner_Tick (0x002D19C8) drives it per frame and Anim_Instance_Ctor (0x003DC1F0) initialises it; the guard reads the clip at self+0x44 and the clip frame-count query 0x0063C78C, so the frame-setter reading is complete. 'Player' is the natural class label for this clip cursor, though the concrete class name is not in the symbol table.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEnemyAiArcAnim
summary: Constructs the eight-slot enemy-AI clip-slot object: base Gfx_BillboardObjectCtorBase, then slot count 8, the arc parameters (0x40A00000 = 5.0, 0xBE4CCCCD = -0.2, 0.5) and the g_animClipSlotArcVtable.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is the named Field_SetupEnemyAi and the installed vtable is the named g_animClipSlotArcVtable, so this is the arc-motion variant of the enemy-AI clip-slot object. Whether 'Anim' is the best noun is unresolved, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_CreateEnemyAiTwoSlotAnim
summary: Constructs the two-slot enemy-AI clip-slot object: base Gfx_BillboardObjectCtorBase, slot count 2, parameter 0x40400000 (3.0) / 0x3E4CCCCD (0.2) and the base g_animClipSlotBaseVtable.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Field_SetupEnemyAi and the vtable is g_animClipSlotBaseVtable, so it is the two-slot sibling of 0x002EBDD8; 'SetTwo' described only the slot count. The object's exact role in the enemy-AI setup is still inferred, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_FinishIconLoad
summary: State handler that completes the asynchronous icon/catalogue load: gets the UI root singleton through 0x006F2224 and calls the named Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad on it.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x00383C18 is the confident Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad and the table word at 0x007298A8 places the function among Ui_Window_GotoState5/9/6Or4 handlers; that table uses the generic Ui_Window state names, so the old 'DiveForm' class attribution is no longer supported and the class prefix is reduced to Ui_Window. The body is a one-call state step.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateRowStateA
summary: Row animation state A: at state 10 updates the row widget/cue and the following row, at state 0x28 rebinds the cue, and after timer 0x3C copies the next state word and hands over to Ui_PanelState_Enter09ForRow.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0072A8B4 is in the Ui_Panel method table 0x0072A8A4 together with maybe_Ui_Panel_SetIconFromList, Ui_Panel_UpdateRowData, Ui_Panel_UpdateRowSelection and the sibling UpdateRowStateB, so the Ui_Panel class is now well supported. The letter A remains because the two row-state handlers cannot be ordered by meaning.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateRowStateB
signature: void maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateRowStateB(u32* state, void* ui, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Row animation state B: at state 0x14 rebinds the row widget, at 0x19 rebinds the cue, and after timer 0x1D inspects the list entry at ui+0xFC/0xFD, optionally rebinds the slot and then writes the next state word.
evidence: NEW: the pointer at 0x0072A8AC is in the same Ui_Panel method table 0x0072A8A4 as maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateRowStateA and Ui_Panel_UpdateRowSelection, so the Ui_Panel class is supported; the exact state semantics remain inferred from the constants 0x14/0x19/0x1D.
